title: Interactive tiling & token affordance library for console density
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a cohesive Figma kit and written guidelines that define an 'interactive tiling' component family and the token affordances that control density, contrast, and micro-interaction behavior across the Redwood Console. Goal is to reduce visual drift between dashboards, rollout rails, and cost views by introducing: a) tiling primitives (cards, lanes, micro-panels) with variant rules; b) a token naming pattern for density, elevation, and interaction states; c) motion recipes for rollouts and collapse/expand behaviors; and d) accessibility color contrasts and focus states. Deliverables: Figma library, token spreadsheet, implementation handoff doc, and a short prototype demonstrating a cost-sparkline + rollout strip interaction with live token toggles.

2026-03-15 - Accessibility audit: preliminary contrast checks passed for text and interactive elements in default/light/dark themes; flagged low-contrast icons inside compact tiles when paired with tertiary background.
2026-03-15 - Aisha: Uploaded prototype and opened design->engineering sync; noted known trade-off: denser tiling increases visual complexity but reduces vertical scrolling for power users.

decisions: Adopt a 4-step density token naming convention: density.{family}.{level} (e.g., density.card.condensed)
Use elevation tokens with semantic names mapped to numeric z-values and CSS variables (elevation.surface.1 -> --elevation-surface-1)
Motion: standardized 120ms entrance, 160ms exit easing for rollouts and micro-expansions; reduce motion in reduced-motion mode
Accessibility: establish minimum 4.5:1 contrast for primary interactive labels inside tiles; provide decorative-icon opacity tokens for low-contrast situations
